title: Barcelona Player Ratings vs. Villarreal: Inspired Comeback Creates Buffer at La Liga Summit
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray10:16 AM ESTBarcelona just about got the job done. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesBarcelona came from two goals behind to achieve an extraordinary 3–2 victory over Villarreal on Sunday, moving them three points clear of Clásico rivals Real Madrid at La Liga’s summit.

Rustiness from the international break was the undeniable culprit responsible for La Blaugrana’s dismal start at Camp Nou, with their visitors two goals ahead in the opening seven minutes. Canadians Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi produced utterly ruthless finishes to stun the home faithful into silence.

Barcelona appeared set to earn a reprieve midway through the first half, but Lamine Yamal clipped the outside of the post with his VAR-awarded penalty kick in windy conditions, as Villarreal narrowly clung onto their two-goal advantage at halftime.

However, despite their defensive deficiencies, Barcelona’s arsenal of attacking weapons came to the party after the restart. Within the space of three second-half minutes, they were back on level terms, with Fermín López’s fizzing strike adding to Gerard Martín’s well-taken header.

The comeback was eventually complete in the 67th minute as Eric García’s cross was turned into his own net by Pau Navarro—who was also sent off in stoppage time—and Barça could have easily glossed the scoreline prior to the fulltime whistle. In the end, their one-goal cushion was enough for three precious points.

Barcelona were blown away early doors. / Josep LAGO/AFP/Getty ImagesAs far as first halves go, Barça have endured few more traumatic under Hansi Flick. Before they had even had time to refamiliarize themselves with the Camp Nou pitch following a fortnight of internationals, they were trailing by two goals—neither of which were particularly pretty viewing for Flick from the touchline.

Villarreal’s opener was beautifully struck by Buchanan, but it was Barça’s hero from the comeback victory over Atlético Madrid before club soccer’s hiatus who gifted them their lead. Fermín López inexplicably passed straight into Buchanan’s feet deep inside his own half, allowing the winger to drive forward and lash beyond Joan García.

Things would get worse just two minutes later. Flick’s recklessly high line was once again unpicked, Villarreal sending Oluwaseyi through on goal with one simple pass. Eric García was no match for the forward’s speed, and his namesake in net was unable to rebuff a vicious effort.

What more could go wrong for Barça? Well, the usually impeccable Yamal decided to add to the chaos, winning and then missing a penalty which would have reduced the deficit and handed momentum to the hosts. The spurned spot kick was one of 15 shots they registered before the break, which yielded a combined 2.08 expected goals, yet they were unable to breach Péter Gulácsi’s goal.

Despite their attacking brilliance, the reigning champions’ disjointed and aggressive defensive line continues to garner unwanted attention. Yamal, Raphinha and Co. can usually spare their blushes—as they did here—but the club’s inability to keep clean sheets could prove their undoing in La Liga against a more competitive Real Madrid team than last year, as well as in the Champions League against some truly formidable opponents.

La Blaugrana have conceded in 11 of their last 14 matches—allowing two or more goals in six of those outings—and that puts their offense under so much pressure to deliver. Luckily, Flick boasts one of the most fearsome forward lines in world soccer.
Yamal (left) was involved throughout—for good and bad. / David Ramos/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Joan García—5.1: Beaten by two fierce strikes and was then untested afterward—apart from one nervy moment when he raced off his line in the dying moments.
RB: Eric García—7.3: Left eating dust as Oluwaseyi motored beyond him to double Villarreal’s lead, but forced the own goal with a teasing delivery across the face of goal.

CB: Frenkie de Jong—7.5: Undermined by those around him early doors during a lesser-seen stint at center back. Excellent at driving the ball forward and stepping through Villarreal’s strict defensive lines.
CB: Gerard Martín—8.1: After some questionable defending and distribution during the opening 45 minutes, Martín began the turnaround with his header just before the hour.
LB: João Cancelo—8.0: Deployed in incredibly advanced positions, creating problems with his technique and creativity. Thwacked the woodwork with an excellent effort on one occasion.
CM: Marc Bernal—7.4: Struggled against Villarreal’s physicality and directness during the first half, but was considerably more assured as the match progressed.
CM: Pedri—8.9: Another elegant performance from the diminutive maestro, who set up Martín’s header and consistently set Barça attacks in motion.
